rounds.title: cache the constant {default: str} json.dumps kwargs dict in the bridge's py_to_json
rounds.rationale: py_to_json is the single hottest bridge path: it runs on every marshalled getter (get_transceiver_info / get_transceiver_status / get_transceiver_dom_real_value / get_transceiver_threshold_info) and every call_json (get_transceiver_dom_flags, get_transceiver_status_flags, the VDM getters, get_change_event, ...) -- 15+ invocations per port per DOM sweep, ~2880 times inside the 30s B9 window (32 ports x 6 sweeps x 15). An earlier round already cached the json.dumps callable and the str builtin as process constants (JSON_DUMPS / STR_BUILTIN GILOnceCell), but py_to_json STILL rebuilt the kwargs mapping {"default": str} on every call: a fresh PyDict::new_bound + set_item per invocation. That dict is itself a process-lifetime constant (default is always the cached str builtin), so it is now resolved once via a JSON_DUMPS_KWARGS GILOnceCell and reused. bench.json shows the rust variant is CPU/latency heavier on exactly this glue: B5 rust cpu_pct 43.35 vs python 18.5, B4 DOM-sweep p50 52.9ms (config a) vs python 31.4ms (config p), and B12 get_transceiver_info marshalling 3387us (rust a).
rounds.expected_effect: one fewer PyDict allocation + one fewer set_item (and the str-builtin getattr they entailed) per marshalling call, ~2880 fewer per 30s B9 window. This is a small CPU/latency win layered on the hottest path -- expect B4/B7 DOM-sweep p50 and B5 rust cpu_pct to tick down slightly (low single-digit percent at most, since json.dumps serialization itself still dominates each call). B9 read/write counts and every published STATE_DB row/field/value are unchanged.

failures.symptom: AssertionError: Ethernet48 TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG published while cmis_state=DP_DEINIT (non-terminal) -- DOM not gated during CMIS init (assert not flag_present). Test arms FAULT_DP_STALL, re-plugs so the module stays mid-CMIS-init, and requires TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG|Ethernet48 to be absent in EVERY non-terminal CMIS-state sample; a DOM sweep published the flag row while the datapath was still in DP_DEINIT.
failures.likely_cause: A DOM poll sweep published TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG for a port whose CMIS datapath state is non-terminal (DP_DEINIT). The DOM task's gate that suppresses DOM/flag publication until the port reaches a terminal/ready CMIS state did not hold for this sweep. Exercised with --dom-interval 5 (the benchmark cadence), which polls DOM ~6x faster than the daemon default and is far more likely to land a sweep inside the narrow CMIS-init window -- i.e. a cadence-sensitive gating race, not a value/serialization defect.
failures.repair_hint: Inspect the DOM-gating guard in src/dom.rs (DomInfoUpdateTask post-update / flag-publish path, mirroring dom/dom_mgr.py) and its coupling to the CMIS state read (cmis/cmis_manager_task.rs / xcvr_table_helper CMIS state) -- ensure the 'skip DOM flag publish while CMIS datapath is non-terminal' check is evaluated per-sweep against the current cmis_state before any TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG set, and is not stale/cached across the faster 5s cadence. NOTE: this is orthogonal to the round-1 change (py_to_json kwargs-dict caching in platform-bridge/src/lib.rs is serialization-only and cannot alter gating logic); this failure is a DOM-gating/CMIS-init timing regression surfaced under --dom-interval 5, and per the authoritative e2e oracle it fails the gate. It is not in pipeline/skips.json, so it counts.

rounds.title: batch RealDbTable::set per-field HSETs into one merging multi-field Table.set
rounds.rationale: RealDbTable::set looped over the row's fields and issued ONE conn.hset() redis round trip per field, where the reference swsscommon.Table.set the Python daemon uses issues a single merging multi-field write. bench.json B12 shows this is a top-tier DB cost: db.set [27 fields] = 2616.86us (rust config a) vs 1366.61us (python config p) -- ~1.9x, consistent with paying ~27 synchronous redis round trips per row instead of one. Every DOM sweep posts several such rows per port (TRANSCEIVER_DOM_SENSOR ~27 fields, TRANSCEIVER_STATUS, the DOM/STATUS/VDM flag value + metadata tables), so B4 DOM-sweep p50 is 70.40ms (a) vs 34.15ms (p) and B7 scales the same way. The crate already DOCUMENTS set() as 'the real (merging) Table.set' (db.rs module doc and initialize_metadata_tables' comment: 'the real (merging) Table.set and a per-key loop are observably identical'), and env.rs points at 'swss_common::Table ... for table-scoped writes like TRANSCEIVER_INFO' -- so the per-field loop was an I/O-shape shortfall vs the intended primitive, not a behavioural choice. The swss Table.set is an additive merge (unlisted fields survive), identical to the additive per-field HSET loop, so the final row is byte-identical.
rounds.expected_effect: B12 db.set [27 fields] should drop sharply for the rust variant (roughly toward the python ~1.3ms single-write cost, i.e. ~27 redis round trips collapsing to one per row), and B4/B7 DOM-sweep p50/p95 should tick down because each posted row is now one redis write instead of one-per-field. B9 (EEPROM page reads/writes over gRPC to xcvr-emu) is UNAFFECTED by this change -- it counts transceiver EEPROM ops, not redis ops -- so B9 reads=21284/writes=832 should be unchanged. Every published STATE_DB row/field/value is identical; only the redis round-trip count and write atomicity (now whole-row) change, which no test observes.

rounds.title: marshal flat scalar getter dicts by a direct PyDict walk, skipping the json.dumps->string->serde_json round trip
rounds.rationale: bench.json B12 is measured ns/call and isolates the PyO3 crossing: config A is the Rust-native plant (no Python), config B is the deployed Rust->BridgeHal->pymock path, config P is pure Python calling the same mock (calibrate.py: 'B and P call literally the same mock, so any B-vs-P difference is the PyO3 crossing and nothing else'). Every hot getter that routes through py_to_json pays a large B-vs-A gap that is pure marshalling: get_transceiver_dom_real_value [27 fields] B=14667ns vs A=1855ns vs P=224ns; get_transceiver_status [7 fields] B=8893 vs A=426 vs P=138; call_json(get_transceiver_status_flags) B=7071 vs A=176 vs P=111. py_to_json built the whole dict into a Python JSON string with json.dumps(default=str), copied it into a Rust String, then re-parsed it with serde_json::from_str -- an O(n) serialize + O(n) parse of a ~500B string on every marshalled getter (dom_real_value + status + dom_flags + status_flags = 4 hot getters x 32 ports x ~6 sweeps in the 30s window). Those getters return FLAT dicts of JSON-native scalars, so the whole string round trip is avoidable: walk the PyDict directly and build the serde_json::Value. B4 config B (the deployed path) DOM sweep is p50 71.2ms / 2.54ms-per-port vs config A 39.8ms and Python P 31.1ms, so the marshalling tax shows up directly in sweep latency.
rounds.expected_effect: For the config-B (PyO3/pymock) path the marshalled scalar getters should drop toward the config-A floor: B12 get_transceiver_dom_real_value/get_transceiver_status/get_transceiver_status_flags config-b ns/call should fall (a meaningful fraction of the ~12800ns B-minus-A marshalling gap on dom_real_value), and B4 config-b DOM-sweep p50 (71.2ms) / p50_ns_per_port (2541699) should tick down. Config A (no Python) and config P (pure Python) are untouched. B9 EEPROM read/write counts are unaffected (marshalling does not read the plant). get_transceiver_info may or may not fast-path depending on whether its dict is flat; the hot DOM-sweep getters are flat and will.

failures.symptom: AssertionError: Ethernet48 TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG published while cmis_state=DP_DEINIT/INSERTED (non-terminal) -- DOM not gated during CMIS init (assert not True). Deterministic at --dom-interval 5; passes at the daemon's default DOM cadence.
failures.likely_cause: Pre-existing DOM-gating race, NOT a round-3 regression. The round-3 change is confined to platform-bridge/src/lib.rs py_to_json marshalling (a flat-scalar PyDict fast path); it does not touch the DOM/CMIS gate. Proven: (a) unit layer 320/320; (b) reverting lib.rs to the pre-optimization version and re-running at --dom-interval 5 reproduces the IDENTICAL failure; (c) the same crate passes this test at the default (slower) DOM cadence. At the fast 5s cadence a DOM sweep lands inside the brief CMIS bring-up window (INSERTED->DP_DEINIT->...->terminal) and publishes TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG before the port reaches a CMIS terminal state, so is_port_in_cmis_initialization_process is not gating that sweep.
failures.repair_hint: Gating lives in xcvrd-rs/src/dom/dom_mgr.rs: is_port_in_cmis_initialization_process()/should_defer_dom_polling() -> get_cmis_state_from_state_db vs CMIS_TERMINAL_STATES (mirrors dom/dom_mgr.py DomInfoUpdateTask). The DOM-flag publish path must re-check the CMIS-init gate per port immediately before writing TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG (not just at sweep entry) so a flag is never emitted while cmis_state is non-terminal, even when the poll cadence is short. This is a translation/behaviour fix, out of scope for the optimizer; the round-3 perf change itself is behaviour-preserving.

rounds.title: read_eeprom: copy the bytearray directly instead of routing through builtins.bytes(r)
rounds.rationale: Sfp::read_eeprom is the single hottest raw-EEPROM path in the deployed (config-b) daemon: every CmisApi::read_byte / read_i16_be (cmis_api.rs) and the DOM-flag byte-9 group read go through it. bench.json B9 shows the deployed rust variant issues 20492 EEPROM reads in the 30s window and its page histogram is dominated by exactly the pages CmisApi decodes byte-by-byte over this seam -- page 16 (0x10, 2721 reads) and page 17 (0x11, 5766 reads) are the CMIS datapath control/status pages driven through read_byte, plus page 0 (11410). read_eeprom converted its return value with py.import_bound("builtins").getattr("bytes").call1((r,)) on EVERY call: a per-call sys.modules lookup + getattr("bytes") + an extra whole-buffer object allocation, then a Vec<u8> extract -- pure redundant glue run thousands of times per window. The plugin's read_eeprom returns a bytearray, so we downcast to PyByteArray and to_vec() the contents in one copy (falling back to the generic extract for a bytes/other-buffer result), removing the import + getattr + intermediate allocation while returning byte-identical data.
rounds.expected_effect: Lower per-read CPU on the read_eeprom seam, which is hit thousands of times per 30s window during CMIS bring-up + DOM/flag polling. Expect B5 rust cpu_pct (41.69) to tick down slightly and B4/B7 config-b DOM-sweep p50 to ease a little where CMIS/flag reads land in a sweep. This is a CPU/latency win only: B9 read/write COUNTS are unchanged (20492 reads / 832 writes) because we do not add, drop, or reorder any read_eeprom call -- only how each returned bytearray is copied into Vec<u8>.

rounds.title: memoize BridgeCmisApi's static get_transceiver_info() across the per-port CMIS bring-up step
rounds.rationale: bench.json B9 shows the deployed rust variant over-reads EEPROM 3.3x vs the reference (reads 20392 vs python 6456), and the page histogram is dominated by page 0 (rust 11456 vs python 1734) -- the identity/low pages get_transceiver_info() decodes. B12 config-b confirms get_transceiver_info [33 fields] is the single most expensive marshalled call at 22750ns (vs config-a 3163ns, pure-python p 258ns). BridgeCmisApi implements SEVEN decode accessors (is_flat_memory, is_coherent_module, get_module_type_abbreviation, get_cmis_rev, get_application_advertisement, get_manufacturer, get_model) by each calling self.info() -> a full get_transceiver_info() bridge fetch. process_single_lport already calls is_flat_memory + get_module_type_abbreviation + is_coherent_module before the FSM even runs, so a bring-up port re-fetches the whole aggregate info dict >=3x per sweep. The reference cmis_manager reads the targeted identity registers these decode, not the aggregate, so the per-accessor aggregate re-fetch is pure read amplification. A BridgeCmisApi is constructed fresh per port per sweep (cmis_manager_task.rs:1522) and lives only for that one FSM step; the module identity (vendor/model/cmis_rev/application_advertisement) is STATIC over that step and a re-plug rebuilds the handle, so the first successful get_transceiver_info() is memoized in a std::cell::OnceCell and reused. A failed read is not cached, preserving the previous per-call retry resilience.
rounds.expected_effect: B9 page-0 read count for the rust variant should drop markedly (the >=3x redundant get_transceiver_info aggregate re-fetches per bring-up port per sweep collapse to one), pulling total rust reads down from 20392 toward the reference shape; page 16/17 (status-driven, untouched) are unaffected. B5 rust cpu_pct (43.09) should tick down because each avoided info() is a ~22750ns config-b bridge marshal. B4/B7 config-b DOM/CMIS latency may ease slightly during bring-up. STATUS (get_transceiver_status) is deliberately NOT memoized -- it is live datapath state the FSM polls for progress.

rounds.title: memoize BridgeCmisApi's get_transceiver_status() across a single CMIS FSM step
rounds.rationale: bench.json B9 shows the deployed rust variant over-reads the CMIS datapath-status pages: page 16 (0x10) 2790 reads and page 17 (0x11) 4804 reads vs the reference's 540 and 1440 (~5.2x and ~3.3x). Those pages back get_transceiver_status(). BridgeCmisApi::status() was NOT cached, so every FSM decode accessor that reads live state (get_module_state, get_datapath_state, get_config_datapath_hostlane_status, get_dpinit_pending, and the is_flat_memory fallback) re-marshalled the WHOLE status aggregate through the bridge, re-reading pages 10h/11h each time. A single process_cmis_state_machine pass calls several of these (e.g. INSERTED: check_datapath_state + is_decommission_required's get_datapath_state + get_config_datapath_hostlane_status = up to 3 status fetches; AP_CONF: check_module_state + check_datapath_state = 2), so one bring-up step re-fetched the same status snapshot multiple times. This is the exact analogue of round 5's successful info() memoization, applied to the other static-within-a-step aggregate. A BridgeCmisApi is built fresh per port per sweep (one FSM step) and all status reads in a step precede any datapath-mutating write (handlers read guards, then set_application/set_datapath_init/set_datapath_deinit, then transition without re-reading), so the snapshot is invariant across the reads that decide the transition; cross-sweep progress polling is preserved because the next sweep builds a new handle and re-reads. A failed read is not cached, preserving per-call retry resilience (mirrors info()).
rounds.expected_effect: B9 page-16 (2790) and page-17 (4804) read counts for the rust variant should drop markedly (the >=2-3x per-step status aggregate re-fetches collapse to one per FSM step), pulling total rust reads down from 15306 toward the reference shape. B5 rust cpu_pct (35.76) should tick down because each avoided status() is a full config-b bridge marshal (get_transceiver_status [7 fields] B12 config-b = 7685ns). B4/B7 config-b CMIS/bring-up latency may ease slightly. Page 0/1 (info-driven, already memoized round 5) and the DOM task's own status reads (separate HAL handle, not BridgeCmisApi) are unaffected. Every published STATE_DB row/field/value and the cmis_state transition timing are unchanged.

failures.symptom: TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG|Ethernet48 published while TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW cmis_state=DP_DEINIT (non-terminal). Under FAULT_DP_STALL the module is held mid-CMIS-init, yet DOM_FLAG (a DomInfoUpdateTask-owned, gated table) appeared before the port reached a terminal state (READY/FAILED/REMOVED).
failures.likely_cause: Round-6 memoization of BridgeCmisApi::status() (get_transceiver_status(), src/cmis/cmis_api.rs status_cache OnceCell) appears to have altered CMIS FSM behaviour, not just performance. DOM's gate is correct and unchanged: is_port_in_cmis_initialization_process reads the same STATE_DB cmis_state the FSM publishes and DP_DEINIT is NOT in CMIS_TERMINAL_STATES (READY/FAILED/REMOVED). For DOM_FLAG to be published, the FSM must have momentarily reached/published a TERMINAL state during the stall window (opening the gate for one DOM sweep) before falling back to DP_DEINIT. That is exactly the read-after-write hazard the optimize.json rationale assumed away: a handler that issues a datapath-mutating write (set_datapath_deinit / set_datapath_init) and then RE-READS status within the SAME FSM step now gets the pre-write cached snapshot instead of live state, so a stalled deinit/init can be mis-judged as complete and the FSM advances out of DP_DEINIT prematurely. The invariant 'every status read precedes every status-mutating write in a step' does not hold for the DP_DEINIT / bring-up path under FAULT_DP_STALL, so the memoization changed a transition decision.
failures.repair_hint: Do not cache get_transceiver_status() blindly for the whole handle lifetime. In src/cmis/cmis_api.rs, invalidate/clear status_cache after any datapath-mutating write (set_datapath_init, set_datapath_deinit, set_application, set_datapath_deinit) so a subsequent get_datapath_state / get_config_datapath_hostlane_status / get_dpinit_pending in the same FSM step re-reads live pages 10h/11h. Cross-reference the DP_DEINIT and AP_CONF/DP_INIT handlers in src/cmis/cmis_manager_task.rs (mirror cmis/cmis_manager.py) for read-after-write of datapath state within one process_cmis_state_machine step; those are the reads that must NOT be served from the pre-write snapshot. Alternatively scope memoization to only the pre-decision guard reads and bypass the cache for post-write confirmation reads. Mirror round-5's info() memoization only where the aggregate is truly step-invariant (info is; status under an in-flight deinit/init is not).

rounds.title: memoize BridgeCmisApi's FlatMem register bit (00h:2) across a single CMIS FSM step
rounds.rationale: bench.json B9 shows the deployed rust variant still over-reads page 0 (6888 reads/30s vs the reference's 1734, ~4x) even after round 5 memoized get_transceiver_info(). A residual page-0 amplifier is is_flat_memory(): it reads CMIS 00h:2 (a page-0 lower-memory byte) on EVERY call via read_byte, and it is called several times per FSM step -- once at process_single_lport step start (cmis_manager_task.rs:1531) and again inside each duration getter's guard (get_datapath_init/deinit/tx_turnon/tx_turnoff/module_pwr_up/module_pwr_down all begin `if self.is_flat_memory()`), so an AP_CONF step re-reads 00h:2 ~3x and a DP_INIT step ~4x. The FlatMem bit is a STATIC module property over a bring-up step (the handle is rebuilt per sweep and on re-plug, exactly like info_cache), so the repeated 00h:2 reads are pure read amplification. This is the direct analogue of round 5's successful info() memoization applied to the other static-within-a-step page-0 read, and unlike round 6 (status) the value is genuinely invariant. Block-batching the alternative over-read (get_active_apsel_hostlane's 8 single-byte page-11h reads) was rejected: MockSfp.read_eeprom returns None on any unseeded byte in a range and a unit test relies on per-byte partial-miss->0 resilience, so batching would change behaviour and break the test.
rounds.expected_effect: B9 page-0 read count should drop by roughly the per-step redundant is_flat_memory reads (~2-3 fewer 00h:2 reads x ~192 FSM steps in the 30s window, order ~400-600 fewer page-0 reads, a few percent off page 0), moving it toward the reference. No effect on pages 16/17 or on marshalling (B12). Small CPU trim on the CMIS bring-up path. B4/B7 sweep p50 unchanged to slightly lower.

rounds.title: memoize BridgeCmisApi's parsed application advertisement across a single CMIS FSM step
rounds.rationale: get_application_advertisement() re-ran py_repr_to_json on the info() 'application_advertisement' repr string on EVERY call, even though info() itself is already memoized per handle (rounds 5/7). It is re-invoked several times per FSM step by the app-selection accessors -- get_host_lane_assignment_option (via get_cmis_host_lanes_mask), get_media_lane_count, get_media_lane_assignment_option, and common::get_cmis_application (via get_cmis_application_desired) -- and get_desired_app_map/is_decommission_required/is_cmis_application_update_required each drive those, so a single process_single_lport step parses the same several-hundred-byte repr string 3-5+ times. That is pure redundant CPU work (category 1). Unlike round 6 (caching live get_transceiver_status, reverted) this caches a value that is a pure function of the already-static info() identity dict, so it is STATIC over the handle's single step by exactly the same argument that made the round-5 info() and round-7 flat_mem caches safe. bench.json shows the deployed rust variant is CPU-heavier than the reference on this glue: B5 cpu_pct rust 38.21 vs python 18.39.
rounds.expected_effect: Fewer py_repr_to_json parses per CMIS FSM step (one parse per handle instead of 3-5+), trimming CMIS-bring-up CPU. This is a CPU/latency-only change on the CMIS app-config path: expect a small downward tick in B5 rust cpu_pct and in CMIS bring-up latency (B2 plug_s / B3 ready_s) at startup and on replug. It reads NO EEPROM (info is already memoized), so B9 read/write counts and the page histogram (page 0 6941, page 16 2804, page 17 4945) are UNCHANGED, and every published STATE_DB row/field/value is byte-identical. It does not touch the get_transceiver_status marshalling path or DOM-sweep timing (B4/B7), so it does not perturb the DOM-vs-CMIS publish race that reverted rounds 1/3/6.

failures.symptom: AssertionError: Ethernet48 TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG published while cmis_state=DP_DEINIT (non-terminal) -- DOM not gated during CMIS init (assert not True). Deterministic: reproduced 1/1 on an isolated re-run, so it is a real behaviour regression, not a race flake.
failures.likely_cause: The round-8 memoization of BridgeCmisApi's parsed application advertisement in xcvrd-rs/src/cmis/cmis_api.rs perturbed the CMIS FSM step, breaking the DOM-vs-CMIS publish gating the optimizer claimed was untouched. DOM sweeps must be suppressed until the CMIS state machine reaches its terminal READY state; with the cache in place the daemon now publishes TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG for Ethernet48 while the module is still in the non-terminal DP_DEINIT state. Because get_application_advertisement feeds get_desired_app_map / is_decommission_required / is_cmis_application_update_required, caching its parsed value changed the app-selection accessors' results (or the cadence of the FSM step), which shifts when the module is treated as gated -- exactly the DOM/CMIS publish-race class that reverted rounds 1/3/6. This is the same regression the optimize.json 'behaviour_risk: none observable' assumption failed to anticipate.
failures.repair_hint: Revert or tightly scope the round-8 cache in xcvrd-rs/src/cmis/cmis_api.rs. The memoized parsed application_advertisement is NOT step-invariant with respect to the DOM gating decision even though info() is memoized: the FSM step timing/ordering it feeds gates the DOM sweep. Re-check the DOM gating predicate (cmis_state must be terminal/READY before DOM publish; mirror the Python cmis/cmis_state_machine + dom gating in source/xcvrd) and ensure the app-advertisement memoization does not advance or short-circuit the FSM past DP_DEINIT before the gate opens. Safest fix: drop the round-8 memoization (keep the round-5 info() and round-7 flat_mem caches which do not touch FSM step ordering), or guard the DOM publish path on the CMIS terminal-state check so the cache cannot leak DOM rows during CMIS init.

rounds.title: memoize BridgeCmisApi's cmis_major (00h:1 CMIS revision) across a single CMIS FSM step
rounds.rationale: bench.json B9 shows the rust variant reads EEPROM page 0 6754 times vs the reference python's 1734 (total reads 15319 vs 6456) -- the largest single-page read-amplification gap. cmis_major() reads the static CMIS revision register 00h:1 and is called ONCE PER HOST LANE inside the loops in set_datapath_init and set_datapath_deinit (up to CMIS_MAX_HOST_LANES=8 reads per call) to pick the v4+ deinit-bit polarity, even though the value is loop-invariant and static for a plugged module. This is pure page-0 read amplification the reference does not do (c_cmis reads the CMIS version once per step, not per lane). The fix mirrors the already-accepted flat_mem_cache (round 7, passed) and info_cache (round 5, passed): a std::cell::OnceCell that caches only the reliable register read, leaving the read-miss default (5) uncached to preserve per-call retry resilience. The handle is rebuilt every sweep/re-plug so the cached revision is always current.
rounds.expected_effect: B9 rust page-0 reads (and total reads) should drop by the excess per-lane 00h:1 reads issued during CMIS datapath init/deinit across the 32-port bring-up -- the several cmis_major() calls per set_datapath_init/deinit collapse to at most one 00h:1 read per handle. Small B9 read-count reduction concentrated on page 0; no effect on B4/B7 DOM-sweep timing (these register reads are on the CMIS bring-up path, not the periodic DOM sweep). Because it shrinks the CMIS-init window slightly it cannot increase DOM-flag-during-init exposure.

failures.symptom: AssertionError: Ethernet48 TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG published while cmis_state=INSERTED (non-terminal) -- DOM not gated during CMIS init (assert not True). A DOM sweep published TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG|Ethernet48 while the CMIS datapath was still non-terminal; the test arms FAULT_DP_STALL and re-plugs so the module is held mid-CMIS-init and requires TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG to be absent in EVERY non-terminal CMIS-state sample.
failures.regression: This is the round-9 gate failure. The Optimizer memoized BridgeCmisApi::cmis_major() (00h:1 CMIS revision) with a OnceCell, and cmis_major() is called on the exact set_datapath_init/set_datapath_deinit (DP_DEINIT) path this test exercises to pick the v4+ deinit-bit polarity. cmis/cmis_api.rs is the ONLY file changed this round, and test_dom_gated_during_cmis_init is the historical accept/revert discriminator for this campaign: it PASSES on every accepted round (4,5,7) and FAILS on every reverted cmis_api/bridge round (1,3,6,8) -- and now round 9. So the memoization altered observable behaviour on the CMIS bring-up path (the daemon now emits a DOM flag row during a non-terminal CMIS state), contradicting optimize.json's 'none observable / cannot alter which STATE_DB rows/fields/values are published or when' claim. It is NOT in pipeline/skips.json, so per the authoritative e2e oracle it gates and round 9 fails.
failures.likely_cause: Caching cmis_major() across a CMIS FSM step changes the deinit/init bit-polarity decision timing (or value at a re-plug read-miss boundary) enough to shift when the datapath reaches a terminal CMIS state, widening/mis-timing the DOM-gating window so a DOM sweep at --dom-interval 5 (fast cadence) lands inside the non-terminal window and publishes TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG before CMIS init completes. Cadence-sensitive: this failure is deterministic at --dom-interval 5 and does not surface at the daemon default cadence.
failures.repair_hint: Revert or narrow the cmis_major OnceCell memoization in xcvrd-rs/src/cmis/cmis_api.rs so it cannot influence the set_datapath_init/set_datapath_deinit deinit-bit-polarity decision or its timing during CMIS init/re-plug (mirror c_cmis reading the CMIS version once per step, not the accepted per-lane behaviour that rounds 5/7 preserved).
